title: The Lone Ranger
paragraphs: A masked Western hero and his companion Tonto travel the American frontier fighting injustice, protecting the innocent, and bringing criminals to the law while guarding the Ranger's identity.
Detroit-originated masked-Western radio drama built around the Lone Ranger and Tonto. Creation is best treated as collaborative: George W.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: WXYZ / Michigan Radio Network launch (January 31, 1933 to October 1, 1934) on [[org|org.4873e07a843601f0|Michigan Radio Network]], Mutual / Earle Graser era (October 2, 1934 to April 7, 1941) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], Graser-Beemer transition (April 9, 1941 to April 16, 1941) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], and Brace Beemer / Mutual era (April 18, 1941 to May 1, 1942) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include George W. Trendle (creator, producer, and writer), [[person|john-todd|John Todd]] (performer), [[person|brace-beemer|Brace Beemer]] (performer, announcer, and commercial spokesman), Fran Striker (writer, editor, and story editor), Fred Foy (announcer, performer, and editor), Charles D. Livingstone (director, producer, and performer), and [[person|earle-graser|Earle Graser]] (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], [[org|org.244a08401c2c9142|WRVR-FM]], and [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].
The stories often return to Outlaws and outlaw gangs, Cattle and ranching, Murder, Rail transport, Horses, and Gold.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes The Lone Ranger and early cooperative radio-network expansion, Children’s radio, cereal sponsorship, and mail-order premiums, and The Lone Ranger across the radio-to-television transition.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|challenge-of-the-yukon|Challenge of the Yukon]], [[show|the-green-hornet|The Green Hornet]], [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|fibber-mcgee-and-molly|Fibber McGee and Molly]], and [[show|the-great-gildersleeve|The Great Gildersleeve]].
